title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, 50, was arrested in July 2025 and jailed about six months after Fargo, North Dakota police accused her of bank theft. She spent nearly four months in a Tennessee jail awaiting extradition and about two more months in North Dakota. The charges were dropped after her lawyer provided bank records proving she was in Tennessee at the time. Lipps is suing the city of Fargo and detective Lucas Heck for $10 million, alleging police relied on an AI facial recognition match from a fake ID and surveillance video, though she did not resemble the suspect and had never been to North Dakota.

The lawsuit claims detective Heck requested an arrest warrant without enough probable cause or further investigation, and that Fargo police lacked policies, training, and supervision for facial recognition use. Lipps says she lost her home, car, and belongings, was denied medications and dentures, and suffered lasting trauma. Fargo officials declined to comment on pending litigation. The suit seeks accountability and damages, but the article does not describe any next steps beyond the court case.
